problems.title: A ratio of two quadratic roots
problems.question: Which listed value is the absolute ratio of roots of x²+2x−8=0?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: The roots are 2 and −4. Their absolute ratio is 2 or 1/2, depending on order. Only 2 is listed.

problems.title: A trapezoid section through its diagonal intersection
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 3,9. Find the parallel cross-section through the diagonal intersection.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: The section length is the harmonic mean $2ab/(a+b)$.
steps: The diagonal intersection lies a fraction a/(a+b) of the height from the base of length a. Linear interpolation gives a+(b−a)a/(a+b)=2ab/(a+b).
With a=3,b=9 the length is 54/12=4.5.

problems.title: Count product roots in the radical domain
problems.question: How many real roots has (x²+13x)(199−x²)√(14−x)=0?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: Domain $x\le14$; a product is zero when at least one defined factor is zero.
steps: Candidates are 0,−13,±√199 and 14. Since √199>14, its positive value is excluded. The other four candidates are valid and distinct.

problems.title: A parallelogram diagonal perpendicular to a side
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals 8,10, and one diagonal is perpendicular to a side. Find its longest side.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: For diagonal vectors p,q, sides are $(p+q)/2,(p-q)/2$.
steps: If the 8-diagonal is perpendicular to a side, the dot-product condition gives |p·q|=8²=64. The squared side lengths are (64+100±128)/4=9,73.
The 10-diagonal cannot be perpendicular to a side: that would require |p·q|=100>8×10, impossible. Thus the longest side is √73.

problems.title: Rectangle width from distance to a diagonal
problems.question: A rectangle has AB=4 and distance from A to BD equal to 2.4. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: In right triangle ABD, altitude to hypotenuse $h=ab/c$.
steps: Let AD=w. Then 4w/√(16+w²)=12/5. Squaring gives 16w²=(144/25)(16+w²), which simplifies to w²=9.
w=3, so perimeter=2(4+3)=14.

problems.title: Count line-parabola intersections
problems.question: How many common points have y=x² and y=x+3?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: D=1+12=13>0, so there are two distinct real x values and two intersections.

problems.title: Add conjugate-denominator fractions
problems.question: Calculate 2/(√18+4)+2/(4−3√2).
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: The combined numerator is 2(4−3√2)+2(4+3√2)=16. Dividing by −2 gives −8.

problems.title: Order three radical quantities
problems.question: Order a=2+√3, b=2√2, c=4.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: Positive quantities may be compared by squaring or by exact bounds.
steps: b≈2.828, a≈3.732, c=4. Thus b<a<c. For exact comparisons, √3<2 gives a<4, and a²=7+4√3>8=b² gives a>b.

problems.title: Leg ratio from a hypotenuse projection
problems.question: One leg’s projection on a right triangle’s hypotenuse is one third of the hypotenuse. Find the leg ratio.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: With p=c/3, the squares are a²=c²/3 and b²=2c²/3. Taking square roots gives a:b=1:√2.

problems.title: Find a circle centre using one auxiliary circle
problems.question: Locate a drawn circle’s centre using a compass and an unmarked straightedge. How many extra circles or arcs are necessary?
problems.idea: Use one circle with a known centre to create two right angles on the original circle.
formulas: An angle subtended by a diameter is 90°; the converse identifies a diameter.
steps: Choose P on the original circle. Draw one circle centred at P, crossing the original at U,V; avoid UV being an original diameter.
Extend UP and VP to opposite auxiliary points E,F. Thus UE,VF are auxiliary diameters; only straight lines are drawn from here onward.
Line VE meets the original again at T. Since UVE=90°, UT is an original diameter. Likewise UF meets the original at S, and VUS=90° makes VS a diameter.
UT and VS meet at the centre. Zero extra circles cannot suffice in general: straight-line constructions preserve projective incidence, which does not determine a Euclidean centre.
problems.note: The printed key marks 2, but this explicit one-circle construction uses only the permitted tools.

problems.title: Rationalize two denominators before multiplication
problems.question: Calculate (√3−1)[1/(√2−1)+1/(√2+√3)].
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: The bracket simplifies to 1+√3. Multiplying by √3−1 gives 3−1=2.

problems.title: A radical rational expression collapses
problems.question: Simplify [(a√a+27)/(√a−√b)]·[(√a−3)/(a−3√a+9)−(√(ab)−9)/(a√a+27)] and evaluate at a=8,b=199.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: Combining the bracket gives [(u−3)(u+3)−(uv−9)]/(u³+27)=u(u−v)/(u³+27).
Multiplying by (u³+27)/(u−v) leaves u, on the original domain a,b≥0,a≠b. At a=8,b=199 all denominators are valid and the value is √8=2√2.

problems.title: Inputs giving the minimum of a reciprocal sum
problems.question: Find the sum of all x minimizing √(x²−2x)/5+3/√(x²−2x).
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: Equality requires t/5=3/t, so t²=15. Thus x²−2x=15, or (x−5)(x+3)=0.
Both x=5 and −3 satisfy the domain. Their sum is 2.

problems.title: Rhombus side from a diagonal and height
problems.question: A rhombus has height 8 and shorter diagonal 4√5. Find its side.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: With d²=80,h=8, squaring dD/2=8s gives 80D²=64(80+D²). Hence D²=320.

problems.title: A numerator root must lie in the denominator domain
problems.question: For which a does (x−a)/√(x−1)=0 have exactly one root?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: The radical denominator must be strictly positive: $x>1$.
steps: A fraction is zero when its numerator is zero and denominator defined. Its only candidate is x=a, valid exactly when a>1.

problems.title: Exclude both numerator roots
problems.question: For which a does (2x²−5x+2)/√(x−a)=0 have no root?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: No root is admissible exactly when neither 1/2 nor 2 is greater than a. This is equivalent to a≥2.
At a=2 the root x=2 is excluded by a zero denominator, so the endpoint is included in the parameter set.

problems.title: Maximize a sum of two roots
problems.question: a+b=5,a>1/2,b>1/2. Find the maximum of √(2a−1)+√(2b−1).
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: Here u+v=2(a+b)−2=8, so the squared expression is at most 16 and the expression at most 4.
Equality holds when u=v, or a=b=2.5, allowed by the strict bounds.

problems.title: Which geometric data can give two different shapes?
problems.question: Compare constructions: I rhombus from a side and acute angle; II right triangle from hypotenuse and altitude to it; III isosceles triangle from base and circumradius. Which can give more than one noncongruent figure?
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: Congruent reflected or rotated copies count as the same shape.
steps: I fixes the rhombus up to congruence. II fixes the two hypotenuse projections as roots of t(c−t)=h²; swapping them only swaps the legs.

III generally permits an acute or an obtuse apex angle subtending the same base chord. These give different isosceles triangles when the base is shorter than the circle diameter. At equality the exceptional right isosceles triangle is unique.
problems.answer: Only III can give two noncongruent figures.

problems.title: Distance between points on opposite sides of a line
problems.question: A,B are distances 3,5 on opposite sides of a line, and their perpendicular feet are 6 apart. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: The normal separation is $3+5=8$; use Pythagoras with the tangential separation 6.

problems.title: A minimum after a square-root substitution
problems.question: Find the minimum of (4x+9)/√x.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: AM–GM gives 4t+9/t≥2√36=12. Equality occurs when 4t=9/t, so t=3/2,x=9/4.

problems.title: Nested radicals become absolute values
problems.question: Evaluate [√(x−2√(x−1))+√(x+2√(x−1))]/√(x²−4x+4) at x=√2.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
steps: At x=√2 we have 0<√(x−1)<1. Thus the numerator is (1−√(x−1))+(1+√(x−1))=2.
The denominator is 2−√2. Rationalizing gives 2/(2−√2)=2+√2.

problems.title: A telescoping radical sum
problems.question: Calculate Σ from n=4 to 8 of 1/[(n+1)√n+n√(n+1)].
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: Each term equals $1/\sqrt n-1/\sqrt{n+1}$ after rationalizing.
steps: The denominator factors as √n√(n+1)(√(n+1)+√n). Multiplication by the conjugate produces the stated difference.
All intermediate terms cancel. The result is 1/√4−1/√9=1/2−1/3=1/6.

problems.title: Two tangent lengths determine centre distance
problems.question: The common internal tangent divides the centre segment in ratio 4:11. Internal and external tangent lengths are 20 and 24. Find centre distance.
problems.idea: Use a precise formula or construction, keeping domains and all valid cases.
formulas: The ratio is also the radii ratio; $L_i^2=d^2-(R+r)^2$, $L_e^2=d^2-(R-r)^2$.
steps: Subtracting gives 24²−20²=4Rr, so Rr=44. Put radii 4t,11t; then 44t²=44, hence radii 4,11.
Now d²=20²+15²=625, so d=25.
